candidate.title: Large-scale CRISPR screening in primary human 3D gastric organoids enables comprehensive dissection of gene-drug interactions.
candidate.abstract: Understanding how genes influence drug responses is critical for advancing personalized cancer treatments. However, identifying these gene-drug interactions in a physiologically relevant human system remains a challenge, as it requires a model that reflects the complexity and heterogeneity among individuals. Here we show that large-scale CRISPR-based genetic screens, including knockout, interference (CRISPRi), activation (CRISPRa), and single-cell approaches, can be applied in primary human 3D gastric organoids to systematically identify genes that affect sensitivity to cisplatin. Our screens uncover genes that modulate cisplatin response. By combining CRISPR perturbations with single-cell transcriptomics, we resolve how genetic alterations interact with cisplatin at the level of individual cells and uncover an unexpected link between fucosylation and cisplatin sensitivity. We identify TAF6L as a regulator of cell recovery from cisplatin-induced cytotoxicity. These results highlight the utility of human organoid models for dissecting gene-drug interactions and offer insights into therapeutic vulnerabilities in gastric cancer.

extraction.results: 鉴定顺铂敏感性相关基因，揭示DNA修复通路转录组趋同，发现蛋白岩藻糖化与顺铂敏感性关联及TAF6L作用

extraction.summary: 建立人胃肿瘤类器官全套CRISPR筛选体系（切割、CRISPRi、CRISPRa、单细胞）。在TP53/APC双敲类器官中筛选顺铂基因-药物互作。鉴定DNA修复通路转录组趋同，发现蛋白岩藻糖化与顺铂敏感性关联及TAF6L在DNA损伤恢复期增殖中的作用。
